features.name: Nothing published until both sign-offs are green
features.label: nothing published until both are green
features.promise: A publish cannot proceed until both the code review (screens 11 and 12) and the outcome sign-off (screen 13) have passed, and the publish carries both.
features.howToVerify: With a change whose code review is approved but whose outcome sign-off is not (and again with the reverse), open the publish step on screen 07 and confirm the destination choices cannot be committed; approve the second one and confirm the same publish then proceeds and shows both sign-offs attached.
features.notes: Flow map edge label 43:91 and the "Choose where it goes" caption 43:40 "Both sign-offs attached".
features.evidence: Both halves can now be given and the gate refuses every incomplete combination. I gave the code half through screen 12's Approve (record: signoffs.code, principal local://user-btc48, sha cbb6995...) and the outcome half through screen 13's 'Sign off on the outcome' (record: signoffs.outcome, written by signOutcome(), which is now wired - verification.vue line 1074). Screen 13 refused the button until every criterion was answered ('2 criteria have not been looked at yet'). Then on screen 07: code approved and outcome missing -> 'The code review is signed off by Default Admin. The outcome sign-off on packet 1 is still outstanding', row not tickable, Publish disabled; outcome approved and code missing -> 'Packet 1 is waiting on both sign-offs', same refusal; both in from two different principals -> chip 'Both sign-offs in' and the dialog listed both with signer and time ('Code review | Is it safe? | Default Admin . approved just now', 'Outcome sign-off | Does it do the job? | Other Person . approved just now'). The last step of the design's script - the publish then proceeding - could not be run, because no GitHub token or repository is configured so no distribution destination is performable at all.

features.name: The brief sits on the main path before the build
features.label: Agree the brief — The need, the open questions, the criteria · Screen 10
features.promise: Agreeing the brief is a required stage between describing what you want (screen 02) and building it (screen 03), unlike checking the diff yourself (screen 04), which is explicitly optional.
features.howToVerify: Create a new extension from screen 02 and confirm the route passes through the brief on screen 10 before the workspace on screen 03; confirm by contrast that screen 04 can be skipped.
features.notes: Flow map: green connectors 43:50 and 43:53 put 43:11 between 43:8 and 43:16 on the main path, while 43:21 marks screen 04 "Optional". Rationale row 44:41: "It is only cheap to catch before the code exists".
features.evidence: Created the w3rc extension from screen 02 (description, outcome, name, 'Draft the brief') and the router went straight to /dashboard/barn/extensions/w3rc/brief - screen 10 - with the masthead 'BRIEF . STEP 1 OF 2 BEFORE ANY CODE IS WRITTEN'. The brief was already on disk in the pod at that point (BRIEF.md holding what I typed plus '## Who asked'), and pressing 'Agree and start building' routed on to /dashboard/barn/editor/w3rc - the workspace - and handed the brief to the assistant as the session's first instruction. Screen 04 by contrast is skippable: nothing routes through it, and I published-dialogued and reviewed from the workspace without visiting it. Worth knowing: screen 10 also offers 'Skip the brief', so the stage is on the path but not compulsory - though skipping now loses nothing, because the brief is written at creation rather than by that screen.

features.name: No capability of the current build is lost
features.label: Keeps everything the current build does: CLI, files, GitHub import, publish, settings.
features.promise: The redesign is additive: the CLI, the files view, GitHub import, publish and settings all remain available, and the raw terminal output in particular is still reachable one click away and still the source of truth.
features.howToVerify: Confirm each of the five capabilities is still reachable in the running Studio, and that the raw assistant output is reachable in one click from the activity stream on screen 03.
features.notes: Cover point one (29:13); rationale row 27:16 "Raw output is still there, one click away, and still the source of truth".
features.evidence: Re-checked all five on a freshly created extension and on base, and the two regressions from last time are gone. CLI: the workspace's Terminal tab is the pod's live tmux session (I read my own prompts back out of it with `tmux capture-pane -t mc-editor`), and the raw output is one click from the activity stream - [data-testid=barn-open-raw-output] labelled 'Open the raw output / the terminal is still here'. FILES: the Files tab lists the tree and the commit history (on a brand-new w3rc: 'd3cd0d4 The seeded extension 23 seconds ago' plus every file), and screen 05 renders. GITHUB IMPORT: 'Import a repo instead' on screen 02 opens the import wizard without leaving the page, and the workspace's publish split menu still carries 'Import from GitHub' beside 'Publish to GitHub' and 'Remove local install'. PUBLISH: both reachable publishes work and are described correctly - the dialog's 'Load into this Rancher' and 'Push the source to GitHub' rows are tickable and marked 'No sign-off'. SETTINGS: /barn/settings carries all of it (What needs sign-off, GitHub connection, What the assistant may do without asking, Where previews run, Who can use Studio, What is sent to the model). The two regressions: (1) the hand-over no longer refuses without a brief - assemblePacket()'s brief check is gone and the record/PR body say plainly when there is none, so 'Push the source to GitHub' works on a brief-less extension again; (2) a refused hand-over no longer moves HEAD - I ticked 'Push the source to GitHub' on w3rc with no token configured and let it refuse, and `git rev-parse HEAD` in the pod read 6cbb9a4968ab26c4be26dd208c62d21d7c172877 both before and after, with the working tree untouched. The dialog copy that used to describe the removed behaviour is also corrected: it now reads 'assembles the work into a packet, pushes that packet to a branch of its own (barn/w3rc/3) in that repository, and opens a pull request against the default branch. Nothing is merged and nothing is written to main.'

features.name: A requested change arrives as an assistant instruction
features.label: Goes straight back to the workspace with the comment already loaded into the assistant — the reviewer never writes the fix themselves
features.promise: A reviewer's comment, from either the code review or the outcome sign-off, is carried into the author's workspace already loaded into the assistant as the instruction to work from, and the reviewer is never asked to write the fix.
features.howToVerify: Comment on a hunk on screen 12 and use "Send to the assistant", then open the author's workspace on screen 03 and confirm the reviewer's exact wording is present as a pending assistant instruction that the author must still approve.
features.notes: Flow map "Changes requested" (43:44/43:46) is fed by amber arrows from both "Code review" (43:82) and "Outcome sign-off" (43:85); rationale row 44:32 adds "the author still approves it".
features.evidence: Drove the whole loop and read the far end. Screen 12's comment composer: typed 'w3rc SEND probe 1787503892 please rename nothing' on product.ts line 26, pressed 'Send to the assistant'; the comment was recorded in barn-review-base with my principal and time, the route became /barn/editor/base?tab=terminal&comment=<id>, editor.vue read the id back with readComment() and the pod's mc-editor tmux pane then held 'A reviewer looked at this change and asked for something. It is about product.ts around line 26. Their words: w3rc SEND probe 1787503892 please rename nothing. Make that change in the working tree and explain what you did.' The record was then stamped sentAt/sentHow='sent', and 'Just record it' leaves it unsent and the thread says so, so delivery is reported rather than assumed. Screen 12's Request changes does the same with its note, and screen 13's per-criterion 'Send this back to the assistant' is the same transport, so a rejection from either reviewer lands in the same place. Two honest gaps: the reviewer's sentence goes straight into the live session rather than arriving staged for the author to approve before it is sent, so 'the author still approves it' is only true of the answer and not of the instruction; and the composer's hint says so plainly rather than pretending otherwise.

features.name: One diff against the last published version
features.label: collapsed into one diff against the last published version
features.promise: The reviewer is shown a single diff of the change against the last published version, not the sequence of intermediate edits that produced it.
features.howToVerify: Make an edit and then undo or supersede it before pushing, then open the change on screen 12 and confirm the diff shows only the net difference from the last published version and no intermediate state.
features.notes: Guardrail note 43:93 on the flow map.
features.evidence: Made an intermediate change and superseded it before the review: in w3rc's pod I committed 'w3rc intermediate: add transient file' creating w3rc-transient.txt, then committed 'w3rc intermediate: remove transient file' deleting it. The baseline ref refs/barn/published/local sat two commits further back. /barn/review/w3rc/working then listed BRIEF.md, pages/Home.vue and verify-w3rc-approve.txt and did not mention w3rc-transient.txt anywhere on the page - the net difference from the baseline, with the intermediate state collapsed out. The mechanism is BASELINE_SH in extensions.ts, which resolves refs/barn/published/oci, then refs/barn/published/local, then HEAD, and every diff on screens 04, 05 and 12 goes through it. Worth knowing: base has no baseline ref at all, so its baseline falls back to HEAD and it is measuring from the last commit rather than from a published version - and no screen says which point it measured from (baselineRef()'s sentence is only consumed by components/BuildFailure.vue).

features.name: Connection state and permission mode are one state shown in two places
features.label: Connection state is a persistent strip in the panel: a dot, the account, and the permission mode as a real control.
features.promise: The account, connection state and assistant permission mode shown on the workspace strip (screen 03) and on the settings page (screen 09) are the same state, and settings is the one place all of it lives.
features.howToVerify: Change the permission mode on screen 09 and confirm the workspace strip on screen 03 reflects it without a reload, and vice versa; confirm no other modal edits the GitHub token.
features.notes: Rationale rows 27:25 ("Screens 03, 09") and 27:34; caption 23:918 "connection, permissions, access and data in one place", replacing the bare token modal (23:919).
features.defect: Neither half of the promise's test can be met. (1) The permission mode is not a control anywhere - the settings card is explicit: 'Not settable, and not per user... these three are drawn as what they are: a statement of the level in force, not a choice.' So it cannot be changed in one place and seen in the other, and the design's 'the permission mode as a real control' on screen 03 does not exist either. (2) A second surface still edits the GitHub token: components/EditorSettingsModal.vue stores and removes it and is opened from screens 02, 03 and 12 (I opened it from screen 12 by clicking the 'No GitHub token' chip). It shares studio-settings.ts with the page so the two cannot disagree, and it deliberately offers only the credential, but the design's caption has screen 09 replacing the token modal outright.
features.evidence: The two surfaces do agree, because they read the same thing: detectPermission() reads the pod's claude-session.sh, so screen 03's strip chip says 'Edits apply without asking' (hover: 'The assistant runs with --dangerously-skip-permissions in this pod') and screen 09's card says the same in longer words and marks that level 'In force'. Settings is also now a real page with all four concerns on it: 'What needs sign-off', 'GitHub connection', 'What the assistant may do without asking', 'Where previews run', 'Who can use Studio', 'What is sent to the model'.

features.name: Verification walks the criteria written in the brief
features.label: Acceptance criteria written in the brief become a checklist walked against the running build, with captured evidence and a second, separate sign-off.
features.promise: The acceptance criteria are authored once on screen 10 and are the same items walked, against the running build and with evidence captured, on screen 13.
features.howToVerify: Write a distinctive acceptance criterion in the brief on screen 10, take the change through to verification, and confirm screen 13 lists that exact criterion as a checklist item, exercised against the running build, with the captured evidence attached.
features.notes: Rationale row 44:59 ("Screens 07 and 13"); caption 45:1206 "the criteria walked against the running build"; flow map 43:37.
features.evidence: Wrote two distinctive criteria into w3rc's BRIEF.md under '## How we will know it worked' ('w3rc criterion one: the tab appears without a reload', 'w3rc criterion two: it says why when metrics are absent'). Screen 13 then listed exactly those two, in order, with Yes/No/Can't tell and a 'Show me' that drives the running preview to the criterion's route. Answering both Yes took the counter to 2/2 and enabled 'Sign off on the outcome'; signing wrote the verdicts back into the same file - '- **Met** at `/home`: w3rc criterion one: the tab appears without a reload' - so the evidence route is captured against the criterion. Screen 12 shows the same items read-only, and base's four criteria appear there with their captured/not-measured states.

features.name: Built from components the dashboard already has
features.label: Everything below is achievable with components that already exist in the Rancher dashboard — SortableTable, LabeledInput, Banner, Card, Tabbed, AsyncButton — so none of this asks the team to invent new UI primitives.
features.promise: Every screen is realisable with existing Rancher dashboard primitives, and the Studio home list in particular uses the same SortableTable pattern as the Clusters page rather than a bespoke table.
features.howToVerify: Inspect the rendered markup of the Studio screens and confirm tables, inputs, banners, cards, tabs and async buttons are the dashboard's own components rather than reimplementations, and that screen 01 reads like the Clusters page table.
features.notes: Header note 27:5 of the rationale frame; rationale row 27:88 names the Clusters page pattern for screen 01.
features.defect: The Studio is built almost entirely on its own primitives: components/ui holds SBadge, SBanner, SButton, SCard, SChip, SEmpty, SField, SIcon, SLabel, SMenu, SModal, SPanel, SRow, STabs, SToolbar, and every one of the ten screens is drawn with those. The only Rancher components imported anywhere in pkg/barn are AppModal, LabeledSelect and AsyncButton, and only in four of the older components (NewExtensionModal, PublishStatus, ExtensionSelect, ExtensionFiles). So Banner, Card, Tabbed and SortableTable are all reimplementations, and screen 01 in particular is a hand-rolled table rather than the SortableTable the rationale names.
features.evidence: Screen 01's list is a bespoke component, not the Clusters page pattern. The element behind .studio-home__table is a DIV grid, there is no .sortable-table anywhere on the page, and grepping pkg/barn for 'SortableTable' or 'ResourceTable' returns nothing. Its headers (State, Name, Source, Running on, Last change) reproduce the pattern by hand.

features.name: A guaranteed way back from any build failure
features.label: When it breaks — plain-language cause, one-click fix, guaranteed way back
features.promise: Every build is snapshotted so that a failure always has a state to roll back to, which means the snapshot has to be taken in the workspace before the change that breaks it.
features.howToVerify: Cause a build to fail from a known-good state and confirm screen 08 offers a snapshot of that state to roll back to, and that rolling back returns the workspace to it.
features.notes: Caption 23:915 and rationale row 27:97 "a snapshot to roll back to"; the snapshot is created on screen 03 and consumed on screen 08.
features.defect: The design's guarantee needs a snapshot taken before every change, and nothing takes one. editor.vue's publishTo() calls recordWorkingBuild() only after a successful LOCAL publish, and that record lives in the browser's own storage, so on a fresh browser, on an extension nobody has locally published, or on the first failing build there is no working-build point at all. The screen is honest about it, which is right, but the promise ('every build is snapshotted so a failure always has a state to roll back to') does not hold. I did not click Roll back: it would have thrown away four other verifiers' work in the shared base pod.
features.evidence: Seeded barn.publish.failure and opened /barn/extensions/base/build-failed. There is a way back and the screen names it, but it is not the guaranteed one the design asks for: it offered 'Roll back to the snapshot "before overwriting w3-files-conflict.txt"' - a snapshot somebody else happened to take by hand 5 minutes earlier, with '4 changed files since' - and the note under it says outright 'What it rolls back to is only as good as the point above: nothing takes a snapshot automatically when a build succeeds yet, so this is the nearest point that exists rather than a guaranteed last working build.' findWayBack() falls back through last-working-build, baseline ref, newest hand-made snapshot, then HEAD, and only the first is actually a build that worked.

features.name: Iteration before the gate asks nobody
features.label: Iteration is completely ungated: dev preview and developer load ask nobody.
features.promise: Creating, building, previewing, breaking, rebuilding and developer-loading an extension never require anyone's approval, so no review or sign-off control may block any of them.
features.howToVerify: Make several edits in the workspace (screen 03), let a build fail and recover it (screen 08), and developer-load the result, confirming that no approval dialog, pending-review banner or disabled control appears at any point before screen 07.
features.notes: Rationale row 65:1083; flow map caption 43:18 "Readable activity, live preview, and no gates at all" and 43:24 "Everything before it is yours alone".
features.evidence: Created w3rc from screen 02, agreed its brief on screen 10, watched it in the workspace on screen 03, opened its diff on screen 04 and screen 12, opened its files, and read its verification on screen 13 - no approval dialog, no pending-review banner and no disabled control at any point. The publish dialog states the rule itself: the 'Load into this Rancher' and 'Push the source to GitHub' rows both carry 'No sign-off' and are tickable, and the note under the sign-offs reads 'Two people answer two questions, and only leaving the gate ... asks for them. Loading this into a Rancher to try it, or handing it over on GitHub to ask for a review, needs nobody.' The settings page's sign-off matrix cannot override this: policyNote() says out loud that a 'required' value on the dev-load row is 'recorded and not obeyed'.

features.name: The OCI publish gate
features.label: Push to an OCI repository — The one hard gate. Everything before it is yours alone · Screen 07
features.promise: There is exactly one hard gate in the whole product and it is the push to an OCI repository, the point at which the extension first becomes installable by other people.
features.howToVerify: From a freshly created extension, walk stages 01, 02, 10, 03 and 04 without ever being asked for an approval, then start a publish to an OCI repository on screen 07 and confirm that this is the first and only step that will not complete on the author's say-so alone.
features.notes: Flow map 43:22/43:24 and the guardrail note 43:93; rationale row 65:1083 states it as "The gate is the push to an OCI repository, where the extension first becomes installable by other people".
features.evidence: There is now exactly one hard refusal in the product and it sits at the distribution boundary. distributeExtension() opens with assertGateOpen(); nothing else can reach a distribution, and the two other ways out of the pod (publishExtension for the local load, handOverForReview for the GitHub push) are deliberately ungated. It is reachable from screen 07 now: I drove the publish dialog on /barn/editor/w3rc through eight hand-written review records and read what it said each time. With no sign-offs: 'Packet 1 is waiting on both sign-offs' and the OCI and repository rows had no checkbox. Code only: 'The outcome sign-off on packet 1 is still outstanding.' Both by the same person: 'Both sign-offs on packet 1 carry the same person, Default Admin...' Two different people: chip 'Both sign-offs in', 'Packet 1 is signed off by Default Admin for the code and Other Person for the outcome.' Walking 01, 02, 10, 03, 04, 05, 12 and 13 beforehand asked for no approval anywhere. Worth knowing: the OCI push itself does not exist and the row says so ('Not built. Pushing to an OCI registry means building a Helm chart from the extension and pushing it with a registry client, and this Studio has neither in the pod and no registry configured'); the performable half of the same boundary is the 'Put the reviewed packet on the repository' row, and that one is also unavailable here because no GitHub token or repository is configured.

features.name: The hand-off to review is a PR, and the PR is the record
features.label: hand-off · the PR is the record
features.promise: Crossing the gate hands the work from the author's lane to the reviewers' lane by producing a PR, and that PR is the durable record of the hand-off.
features.howToVerify: Push a change to an OCI repository and confirm the resulting queue entry on screen 11 is backed by a PR, and that the PR is reachable from the review surface as the record of the change.
features.notes: Flow map connector label 43:90 on the green connector running from "Push to an OCI repository" (43:22) into "Code review" (43:28).
features.defect: Two gaps. (1) Screen 12's PR chip cannot find the PR the hand-over makes: checkPullRequest() searches for an open PR whose head is listBranches().current, but a packet's branch is created with `git branch -f` and never checked out, so the branch it searches for is never the packet's. The only reader of packets[n].pr in the product is PublishModal's gatePacketPr(), which is on screen 07, not on the review surface. (2) Unverifiable end to end in this environment: the barn-settings Secret holds no GitHub token and no repository is remembered, so the hand-over refuses before it reaches GitHub and no queue entry can be backed by a PR.
features.evidence: The hand-over is built to produce the PR and the record is written, but nothing can read it back to a reviewer and no PR can be made here. handOverForReview() assembles the packet, pushes branch barn/<ext>/<n>, opens the pull request and stores {branch, sha, base, pr, prError, pushError} in the review record; the GitHub dialog now describes exactly that ('assembles the work into a packet, pushes that packet to a branch of its own (barn/w3rc/3) in that repository, and opens a pull request against the default branch. Nothing is merged and nothing is written to main'), so the stale 'pushes straight to main' copy is gone.

features.name: Preview and published are separated by an explicit line
features.label: The same live preview, plus an explicit boundary: preview is yours alone, snapshotted per build, and publishing is a separate deliberate act.
features.promise: Work in the live preview affects only the author and is snapshotted per build; nothing reaches anyone else until the separate, deliberate publish on screen 07.
features.howToVerify: Make a visible change in the workspace preview on screen 03, then confirm from another session or another user that the installed extension is unchanged until a publish is performed on screen 07.
features.notes: Rationale row 27:52 ("Screens 03, 07"); the cover's reading note 29:41 calls it "an explicit line between preview and published".
features.evidence: base's pod has six files changed in its working tree and its dev-server preview renders them (screen 12's 'Rendered result' panel reported 'Loaded . just now' against http:barn-base-extension:8005/proxy), yet nothing named base exists in uiplugins.catalog.cattle.io - the only two are barn and nodehealth. Every Studio surface says the same thing rather than blurring it: screen 12's masthead reads 'base . not published yet', screen 04's action bar reads 'These changes are running in your preview only', screen 01's row reads 'local (preview)' under Running on, and the publish dialog separates 'Load into this Rancher' (which does reach everybody signed in here) from the preview. Publishing stays a separate deliberate act behind its own confirmation.

features.name: Prompt provenance and the brief survive from authoring into review
features.label: Every hunk carries the prompt that produced it, and the whole change carries its brief.
features.promise: The prompt that caused each hunk is captured during authoring on screen 03 and is still attached, per hunk, when the change is reviewed on screen 12, and the brief from screen 10 travels with the change as a whole.
features.howToVerify: Author a change with two distinguishable prompts in the workspace, push it, then on screen 12 confirm each hunk shows the prompt that produced it and that the change header shows the brief written on screen 10.
features.notes: Rationale row 44:5; caption 45:1204 "prompt provenance per hunk".
features.evidence: Both halves work and I saw the join. Capture: pressing 'Agree and start building' on w3rc's brief put a record in the pod's /app/.barn/provenance.jsonl carrying the prompt, screen and principal - {"kind":"prompt","turn":"tmt61m5036hlol","prompt":"Read BRIEF.md in this package...","screen":"workspace","principal":"local://user-btc48","who":"Default Admin"} - so authoring provenance is captured with the person attached. Survival: with a completed turn on record (a commit carrying a Barn-Turn trailer plus its turn record), `node /seed/barn-provenance.mjs report` resolved the hunk by blame and screen 12 rendered it per hunk: 'Prompt 1 of 1 / w3rc audit prompt: colour the greeting so a pressure event stands out / 3 lines . 1 minute ago / See the conversation', with the change-wide summary '1 prompt behind this change'. The brief travels too: screen 12's left column renders w3rc's BRIEF.md as the packet - what this is for, who asked, the problem, what changes, where it appears, and its criteria. Caveat worth recording: the pod's claude is signed out, so no turn ever ends by itself (the Stop hook never runs) and every real hunk reads 'N lines changed in the pod, no prompt recorded'. I had to write the turn record and the trailer commit by hand to exercise the join; everything downstream of that - the report, the overlap match between the -U0 report and the -U3 display, and the strip - is the product's own.

features.name: Live is reversible from the extension list
features.label: Reversible from the extension list
features.promise: Publishing is not a one-way door: a live extension can be taken back from the Studio home list on screen 01.
features.howToVerify: Publish an extension, return to /dashboard/barn/extensions, and confirm the row for the live extension offers a way to reverse the publish.
features.notes: Flow map terminal state "Live" (43:41) and its caption 43:43; the reversal control lives on screen 01, not on screen 07.
features.evidence: Opened the row menu for nodehealth on /barn/extensions - the one extension that is actually installed (Running on 'catalog . v0.1.0'). The menu offers 'Remove the local install' enabled and annotated with the version it would take off ('v0.1.0'); on the rows that are not installed the same item is disabled with the note 'not installed'. It is wired to removeLocalInstall(), which deletes the UIPlugin and reports 'is no longer loaded by this Rancher. The extension itself is untouched.' I did not press it: nodehealth belongs to another verifier's fixture and the brief forbids publishing, and the promise as written is that the row offers the reversal.

features.name: Every recovery route returns to the same workspace
features.label: amber is recovery — and every recovery route leads back into the same workspace rather than out of the product
features.promise: Both failure routes drawn on the map, a broken build and a rejected review, end back in the author's workspace rather than in a separate remediation surface or outside the product.
features.howToVerify: Trigger a build failure and apply its fix, confirming the user lands back in the same workspace; separately, request changes as a reviewer and confirm the author is returned to that same workspace rather than to a new screen.
features.notes: Flow map legend 43:4; the amber arrows 43:62/43:65 leave and re-enter the same "Build it and watch it" box (43:16), and "Changes requested" (43:44) routes back to it.
features.evidence: Both amber routes end in the same workspace. Changes requested: screen 12's Request changes on w3rc recorded the refusal and routed to /dashboard/barn/editor/w3rc?tab=terminal, and the reviewer's sentence was in that pod's assistant pane when I read it; the comment composer's 'Send to the assistant' does the same via /barn/editor/base?tab=terminal&comment=<id>; screen 13's per-criterion 'Send this back to the assistant' uses the same askAssistant transport. Build failure: screen 08's controls are 'Ask the assistant to explain this', 'Ask the assistant to fix it', 'Show me pages/NodeHealth.vue', 'Roll back to the snapshot ...' and 'Undo the last change' - all of which act on the same pod and return to the same workspace rather than opening a separate remediation surface or leaving the product.

features.name: The review packet accumulates in the background and is assembled at the push
features.label: the review packet accumulates quietly in the background. It is only assembled and handed to a reviewer at the push to a repository
features.promise: Everything a reviewer will need is captured continuously while the author works, but it is only assembled into a review packet and handed over at the moment of the push.
features.howToVerify: Work in the workspace for several build cycles without publishing and confirm nothing appears in the review queue (screen 11), then push once and confirm a complete packet, including material captured across all of those earlier cycles, appears in a single queue entry.
features.notes: Guardrail note 43:93 on the flow map.
features.defect: A dirty working tree still puts an extension in the review queue. base and w3rc have both never been handed over, and /barn/review counted 'Waiting on you 2' with both of them listed - the row explains the state in words but it is still a row in somebody's queue, so 'work for several build cycles without publishing and confirm nothing appears in the review queue' does not hold. review-queue.vue's load() enumerates every extension and enriches it, rather than enumerating packets.
features.evidence: The 'assembled at the push' half is right: assemblePacket() allocates refs/barn/packets/<n>, attaches the blame-resolved provenance index as a git note and creates branch barn/<ext>/<n>, and its only caller is handOverForReview(). What accumulates in the background is real too - /app/.barn/provenance.jsonl gains a record on every prompt the Studio sends, with the screen and the principal on it - and the queue now reads packets: distributionGate() and sinceLastLook() are called per row and the row for a change with no packet says 'Never handed over, so nobody has been asked to review it. It is still the author's own working tree.'

features.name: The build is compared back to its own brief at sign-off
features.label: The build is compared back to its own brief, and anything outside it is flagged during sign-off — accept it into the brief, or take it out.
features.promise: At outcome sign-off the built change is diffed against the brief that started it, and anything not in the brief is surfaced with two resolutions: accept it into the brief, or remove it.
features.howToVerify: Have the assistant make a change beyond what the brief asked for, take it to screen 13, and confirm the extra work is flagged as outside the brief and offers both accepting it into the brief and taking it out.
features.notes: Rationale row 44:68; requires the screen 10 brief to still be attached to the change at screen 13.
features.defect: Neither resolution the design asks for exists. The drifted branch of the Scope card renders a warning banner and a list of term/file rows and nothing else - there is no 'accept it into the brief' control that would add the work to the brief, and no 'take it out' control that would revert it. The check is also a term match over added lines rather than a comparison of the build against the brief, so work that is outside the brief but does not reuse a non-goal's words is not flagged at all.
features.evidence: Detection works and is honest about what it is. Screen 13's Scope card went from 'The brief does not say what this was deliberately not doing' to 'This change adds lines that mention what the brief said it was deliberately not doing. features.name: Re-review is incremental across visits
features.label: A "since your last look" filter, and a banner on the queue row saying how many changes landed since you approved.
features.promise: Per-reviewer state persists between visits, so a reviewer returning after the author has pushed again sees how many changes landed since they approved and can filter the diff to just those.
features.howToVerify: Approve a change as a reviewer, push further changes as the author, then return to screen 11 and confirm the queue row banners the number of changes since that approval, and that screen 12 offers a "since your last look" filter restricted to them.
features.notes: Rationale row 44:23, "Screens 11 and 12".
features.defect: The second half of the promise does not exist: there is no way to filter the diff to what landed since. The banner says so itself ('The diff below is still the whole change rather than only the newer part of it: narrowing it needs a diff taken against the commit you last read, and nothing in the Studio takes one against an arbitrary commit yet'), and arriving from the queue's link with ?scope=since produces a warning banner naming the commit it would have measured from instead of a narrowed diff. Every diff in extensions.ts is pinned to $BARN_BASE, so the missing piece is a diff function that takes an arbitrary base.
features.evidence: The per-reviewer half is real and persists. markLook() now runs on every screen-12 load: barn-review-w3rc gained looks.pa5g3hz = {principal: local://user-btc48, name: Default Admin, packet: 1, sha: 4926d49, at: ...}, keyed by a hash of my principal rather than to the extension. After a second packet was handed over, reloading /barn/review/w3rc/working showed '1 change landed since you last looked at packet 1.' and the queue reads the same sinceLastLook() per row.

features.name: Two sign-offs by two different people
features.label: Splits "is it safe?" from "does it work?" — two questions, two people, neither able to answer the other's.
features.promise: The code review is signed by a developer and the outcome sign-off by the person who asked for the change; they are separate acts by separate roles, not one approval recorded twice.
features.howToVerify: Confirm the code review record (screen 12) and the verification record (screen 13) carry distinct signer identities and distinct timestamps, and that signing one does not mark the other complete.
features.notes: Rationale row 44:59; flow map 43:32 "A developer" and 43:37 "The person who asked"; cover point three 29:21 "a separate outcome sign-off by the person who asked".
features.evidence: The two sign-offs are separate acts with separate records and the product refuses one person giving both. signCodeReview and signOutcome write independent entries carrying the Rancher principal from currentSigner(); on w3rc I produced both through the real screens and got two entries with distinct timestamps (code 17:02:16, outcome 17:07:09) that did not affect each other - approving the code left the outcome dot empty and signing the outcome left the code entry alone. The role split is enforced rather than described: signOutcome() reads the brief's '## Who asked' section and refuses anybody else, and screen 02 now writes that section at creation ('## Who asked / local://user-btc48 - Default Admin, on 2026-08-23' in w3rc's BRIEF.md), so screen 13 said 'The brief records you as the person who asked for this, so the outcome sign-off is yours to give.' With both entries carrying the same principal the gate refuses: 'Both sign-offs on packet 1 carry the same person, Default Admin. The two questions are "is it safe?" and "does it work?", and they are two sign-offs precisely because one person answering both is one opinion recorded twice.' With two different principals it opens. Nothing checks that the code reviewer is a developer, and the product does not claim to.

features.name: Use Shift + Enter for a new line

Shift+Enter inserted \n into the textarea and did not send (turn count held at 28). Enter alone sent: field cleared, a new user bubble appeared, and the pod recorded the prompt seconds later. The second half of the hint holds too - nothing in sendToAssistant/askAssistant touches publishExtension.

features.name: Discard every change

features.notes: Button/Ghost with icon/trash. Destructive; check for a confirmation.
features.defect: The screen does not empty afterwards, and it cannot, because it counts against a different point from the one it discards to. The file list is `changedFiles`, measured from $BARN_BASE (refs/barn/published/oci, then refs/barn/published/local, then HEAD), while discardChanges() puts the working tree back to HEAD. On w3rc, which has a baseline ref two commits behind HEAD, the list still showed the same three files after the discard, the action bar still said '3 of 3 files will be kept' and the badge still read Unsaved - so a user is told 'this cannot be undone', it is done, and nothing on the screen changes. Also worth naming: two of those three files were only different from the baseline because of commits, and 'Discard all' cannot touch a commit, so the button's own label over-promises on any extension that has ever been published or handed over. On base, which has no baseline ref, baseline resolves to HEAD and the two readings agree, which is why this did not show up before.
features.evidence: Drove it on my own extension. /barn/extensions/w3rc/review listed 3 changed files (BRIEF.md, pages/Home.vue, verify-w3rc-approve.txt) with the button reading 'Discard all'. Clicking it asked first - window.confirm received 'Discard all 3 changed files in w3rc? This cannot be undone.' - and the discard itself really happened: `git status --porcelain` in the pod went from ' M BRIEF.md / M pages/Home.vue' to empty.

features.notes: Heading text is "GitHub connected" (15:545).
features.defect: githubApiAnywhere() in extensions.ts (~line 2925, and githubApi() at ~2857 has the same line) builds a node -e script containing the literal regex /[\r\n]+/g. The TypeScript source doubles the escapes correctly, but the built bundle in dist-pkg/barn-0.5.22 carries them singly, so at runtime the emitted script has real CR/LF inside the character class and node never reaches the fetch. Neither githubIdentity() nor listGithubRepos() can succeed with any token, valid or not. Avoid a regex literal with escapes inside the emitted script (for example replace(/\s+/g, ' ') written without backslash escapes, or String.raw), and check the built artifact rather than only the source.
features.evidence: Step 1 is wired to githubIdentity() now - the code calls it on mount and on connect - but it can never answer, so the row shows no handle, no scopes and no expiry. With a token stored, [data-testid=barn-import-account] read: 'A token is stored, so a private repository clones too. Studio could not read the account from it: " + String(e.message).replace(/[' with barn-import-account-login and barn-import-account-meta both absent. That trailing text is a fragment of the pod script's own source leaking through as the error message. Root cause reproduced in the pod: the installed bundle emits the node script with a REAL carriage return and line feed inside a regex character class (the bundle's string literal is '...replace(/[\r\n]+/g, " ")...' with single backslashes, so the value contains the control characters), node dies with 'SyntaxError: Invalid regular expression: missing /' and echoes the offending source line, and the caller's /BARN-GH-ERR:(.*)/ then matches that echo instead of a real error. Ran the same one-liner via kubectl exec into barn-base-extension and got exactly that SyntaxError and exactly that echoed line.

features.name: See which GitHub account is connected
features.label: Connected as kwwii
features.promise: The card shows the connected account, an Active pill, the granted scopes, the expiry and the authorisation date.
features.howToVerify: Open the Studio settings screen (the gear in the rail, or /barn/settings if it exists), connect a GitHub account and check the card shows the login, the Active pill, the scopes and both dates.
features.notes: Account frame 21:828, pill 21:834 'Active', detail 21:836. Pill 21:835 reads 'Active'; detail 21:836 reads 'Scopes: repo, read:org · expires 18 Oct 2026 · authorised 12 Aug 2026'.
features.defect: pkg/barn/extensions.ts:2898 - the injected script's last line is written as '...String(e.message).replace(/[\r\n]+/g, " ")...' inside a single-quoted TS string, so the emitted script contains a literal newline inside the character class and never compiles. githubIdentity() therefore always throws, which means (a) login/scopes/expiry are never read from GitHub, (b) the chip can never be 'Active' and can never be 'Rejected by GitHub' either, because a SyntaxError is not a 401 and `rejected` tests for /\b40[13]\b/, and (c) a node SyntaxError echo is printed into the UI as an explanation. Escape it (\\r\\n) or use /\\s+/ built from a string. listGithubRepos() goes through the same helper and is broken the same way. Separately: the card claims 'the credential itself never comes back into this page', and that is false - readToken() GETs /k8s/clusters/local/v1/secrets/barn/barn-settings from the browser and base64-decodes it; I captured that response three times in one page load with gh_token in the body.
features.evidence: The pod-side identity read is broken, so none of GitHub's own answers ever reach the card. Seeded Secret barn-settings with a placeholder token (never a real credential) and reloaded: the row read 'A token is stored' with the chip 'Unverified' and the detail 'Nothing could ask GitHub about it just now: " + String(e.message).replace(/[. Anything above it is what was recorded when it was stored.' - the error text is a fragment of the script's own source. Seeded ConfigMap barn-studio-settings with a recorded connection as well and reloaded: 'Connected as w3-settings-probe / Scopes: repo, read:org . stored 8/23/2026', still chipped 'Unverified', and the word 'expires' appears nowhere on the page. Reproduced the cause directly in the pod: the script githubApiAnywhere() injects ends with .replace(/[\r\n]+/g, " "), and \r\n in the TS string literal become real CR/LF characters, so the pod's node exits with 'SyntaxError: Invalid regular expression: missing /' before any fetch runs. The same fetch written by hand in the same pod returns 401 Bad credentials, so egress is fine.

features.howToVerify: Open the Studio settings screen (the gear in the rail, or /barn/settings if it exists), read the GitHub connection card head and confirm it names both uses and the isolation promise.
features.notes: Head 21:825, description 21:826. Description 21:826 reads 'Used to import repositories and to open pull requests when you publish. Extensions never see this credential.'
features.defect: The design's promise (a generated extension never gets this credential) is not true here and the card declines to make it. Making it true means running extension pods under a ServiceAccount that is not cluster-admin, or keeping the token out of a namespace those pods can read.
features.evidence: The card names both uses - 'Used to import repositories and to push when you publish' - and then states the opposite of the design's isolation promise, correctly: 'Generated extensions are never handed this credential, but the pod they run in can read the Secret it lives in (barn-settings in namespace barn, and that pod is bound to cluster-admin)'. Verified the binding: `kubectl get clusterrolebinding barn-extension-cluster-admin` is roleRef cluster-admin over ServiceAccount barn/barn-extension, which is the ServiceAccount every extension pod runs as.

features.notes: Only the sentence is drawn, in the link colour (#8B8B96 body but styled as a hint). No field and no button for it exists in the frame, so the control that accepts the token is inferred.
features.evidence: Clicking Connect reveals SField 'GitHub token' (type=password, data-testid settings-github-token) and focuses it, with the hint 'A personal access token with the repo scope is enough' and a link to https://github.com/settings/tokens/new?scopes=repo&description=Rancher%20Extension%20Studio. Drove it for real with a placeholder token: pressing Enter spent it against api.github.com from the browser, GitHub answered 401, the field went into its error state and Secret barn-settings was left with no data at all - so a rejected token is refused rather than stored. The card also states plainly that the design's per-user storage does not hold: 'there is one Secret for this Rancher's Studio and everybody using it uses the same credential.'

features.name: Understand that iteration is never interrupted

features.notes: Title 62:1187; body 62:1188: 'While you build, changes accumulate against the last published version. There is no per-change approval, no notification, and nothing to click. At the push, the whole run is collapsed into one diff against that version - forty prompts become the three files that actually differ. "Notified" means the person who asked gets the criteria checked against the build; it never blocks the push.' This is the definition of the middle value of every segmented control on this card.
features.evidence: The note at the foot of the sign-off card (data-testid settings-iteration-note) is titled 'Nobody reviews the same extension forty times' and makes all three claims: changes accumulate against the last published version, there is no per-change approval and nothing to click, and at the push the run is collapsed into one diff. It ends 'Notified means the person who asked gets the criteria checked against the build; it never blocks the push', which matches what the publish dialog does with a Notified value - with dev-load.outcome=notified the row's requirement chip became 'Sign-offs advisory' and the row stayed publishable.

features.defect: review-queue.vue changesSince(): `const at = commits.findIndex((h) => h.ref === code.sha)`. listHistory() formats commits with %h (abbreviated) while sign-offs store the full object id, so findIndex always returns -1 and every real sign-off gets the 'the branch has moved past the commit you approved' clause - false when it has not moved, and it also makes the 'never a banner about nothing' condition (at===0 && !changes) unreachable, so a signed-off change with a clean tree gets a banner claiming a move that never happened. gateFrom() already has sameCommit() for exactly this comparison; changesSince should use it.
features.evidence: The banner exists and can be right: with a code sign-off naming an OLDER commit in abbreviated form (ea04b8d) demo's card was topped with [data-testid=queue-since], the undo icon and '2 commits since W3 Other Reviewer approved this on 2026-08-23.' plus the filter link, which is the true count. But sign-offs the product itself writes are 40-character shas (signCodeReview -> resolveCommit expands them), and changesSince() compares them with listHistory()'s %h (7 characters) using ===, so they never match. Proved it both ways on the same record: sha '22db7ed191e63bc644e4f9a5ed892a918f9fb232' (demo's actual HEAD, clean tree) produced a banner reading 'the branch has moved past the commit you approved since W3 Other Reviewer approved this on 2026-08-23'; the identical record with sha '22db7ed' produced no banner at all, which is correct.

features.name: Yes / No / Can't tell verdict per criterion
features.label: Yes
features.promise: For every criterion the reviewer picks exactly one of three verdicts: Yes, No, or Can't tell.
features.howToVerify: Click each of the three segments on a criterion, confirm only one stays selected, that the selection colour matches (Yes green, No red, Can't tell grey), and that the progress chip and the footer message update.
features.notes: Segmented control repeated per criterion: 39:1232 (crit 1, Yes selected, #3E8C4F), 39:1257 (crit 2, Yes), 39:1284 (crit 3, No selected, #F64747), 39:1325 (crit 4, Can't tell selected, #F2F3F5 grey). Unselected segments are white. No 'unanswered' state of the control is drawn: every criterion in the mock carries a verdict.
features.evidence: Each criterion has three segments with role=group. Clicking Yes on criterion 3 set aria-pressed=true on Yes and false on the other two; clicking No moved it to No only; clicking Can't tell moved it to Can't tell only - never more than one at a time. The selected colours are Yes green (badge rgb(62,140,79), card untinted), No red (badge rgb(246,71,71), card background rgb(253,236,236)), Can't tell warning amber (badge rgb(201,162,39), card untinted). The progress chip and the footer moved with every press: "3 of 4 met, 1 still to look at" -> "2 of 4 met, 1 not met, 1 still to look at" -> "2 of 4 met, 1 could not be judged, 1 still to look at". Pressing the pressed segment again clears it back to unanswered.

features.name: Can't tell is a first-class, non-blocking verdict
features.label: Can't tell
features.promise: A criterion that can be neither passed nor failed is answered 'Can't tell': it is styled neutrally (grey, not red), it is excluded from the 'checked' count, its number badge stays a plain number rather than a tick or a cross, and it does NOT block publishing - only a 'No' does.
features.howToVerify: Set a criterion to 'Can't tell' and confirm three things: the counter does not increment, the footer still reports only the 'No' criteria as blocking, and the badge shows the criterion number in grey.
features.notes: Read from four drawn signals: the grey selected fill #F2F3F5 on 39:1330; the badge 39:1316 being a grey circle containing the literal '4' while badges 1-3 are icon glyphs on green/green/red; the counter saying '3 of 4 checked'; and 39:1313 saying 'Publishing is blocked while any criterion is No'. Criterion 4's evidence line explains why it cannot be answered: 'Nothing here has fifty nodes. Needs a real cluster.'
features.evidence: Set criterion 3 to Can't tell and checked all four claims. The counter did not increment (3/4 -> 2/4 when Yes became Can't tell). The footer reported it separately from a No: "2 of 4 met, 1 could not be judged, 1 still to look at." The badge stayed the plain criterion number "3" with no tick and no cross. And it does not block: with the other three answered Yes and this one Can't tell, the footer read "3 of 4 met, 1 could not be judged. Nothing is holding the sign-off open." and "Sign off on the outcome" was enabled - where a single No disables it with "1 criterion is answered No." One divergence worth recording: the badge is warning amber rgb(201,162,39), not grey. It is not red and not the Yes green, and grey rgb(242,243,245) is kept for "nobody has looked at this", which is the distinction the screen is built around.
